properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js (SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512 implementations) is a runtime dependency of elliptic, which is what secp256k1 uses in the browser build — these hash implementations ship in the production bundle. No direct call site in app code; presence is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 available in the shipped library: 'import CryptoJS from crypto-js' (Save.vue:38) bundles crypto-js's entire module set (MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4, Rabbit included). No MD5 call site in the application. Changeable here — replace/upgrade crypto-js or import only the needed modules.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 available in the shipped crypto-js bundle alongside the modules the app actually calls (PBKDF2, AES, SHA3, SHA256). No SHA-1 call site in the application; changeable by replacing or narrowing the crypto-js import.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Core wallet-generation primitive: secp256k1@5.0.0 native package; publicKeyCreate(privateKey, false) in the inlined generation worker derives the public key for every candidate wallet. In the webpack browser build secp256k1 resolves to its declared runtime dependency elliptic@6.5.4 (pure-JS ECDSA on secp256k1). Quantum-vulnerable under Shor, but the curve is fixed by the Ethereum protocol — changeable only with the ecosystem, not by this app alone.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live by indirection: secp256k1@5.0.0 lists elliptic ^6.5.4 as a runtime dependency (package-lock.json:13023) and resolves to it in the browser build, so elliptic's ECDSA-on-secp256k1 is the code that actually executes when vanity.js calls secp256k1.publicKeyCreate. The collector saw only the lockfile; reachability is via secp256k1's browser fallback. Quantum-vulnerable; curve fixed by the Ethereum protocol.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js (pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 family) is a dependency of create-hash/create-hmac inside the crypto-browserify tree that webpack 4's node-libs-browser wires in for require('crypto'). Declared in the lockfile (dev-flagged tooling chain); no direct app call site — the app's SHA-256 use runs through CryptoJS.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The elliptic package itself — the same logical asset as ALG-710f61f0 (ECDSA via elliptic), reached under both the library facet and the algorithm facet. Live in the browser bundle through secp256k1's browser fallback.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-only (dev: true in the lockfile): generates the self-signed HTTPS certificate for the webpack dev server during local development; never ships in the production bundle. Backed by node-forge (covered by the separate node-forge / X.509 self-signed objects). Changeable here by upgrading the dev-server toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The hash.js package itself — the same logical asset as ALG-50e53f84 (SHA family via hash.js@1.1.7), reached under both the library facet and the algorithm facet.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The browserify pbkdf2 polyfill package, part of the crypto-browserify chain webpack 4 wires in for require('crypto'). The app's keystore PBKDF2 runs through CryptoJS instead; no call site for this package. Changeable only with the build tooling.
